answers.q: Which wildlife is seized most often?
answers.a: Parrots & songbirds lead the public record with 294 cases, then turtles & tortoises (234) and elephant (ivory) (218).
answers.limit: Cases count reporting, not trafficking volume: well-covered species and countries look bigger.

answers.q: Where does seized wildlife come from, and where is it caught?
answers.a: Leaving the United States aside, the busiest seized route is India to China (333 shipments); US-bound routes are 83% of all 24,786 seized shipments reported to CITES.

answers.limit: Countries report seizures unevenly; the United States reports far more completely than most.

answers.q: Is wildlife sold online ever caught?
answers.a: Rarely, in the public record: Bears in Thailand drew 1,303 adverts and 0 WildTrace cases in the same period.

who.name: ECO-SOLVE (Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime)

answers.limit: Adverts and cases are recorded with different effort; the ratio is not a detection rate.

answers.q: How often does a seizure end in a conviction?
answers.a: In the public record, for every conviction there are about 11 seizures: 1,232 seizures, 566 arrest reports and 111 convictions.
answers.limit: Courts are reported far less than seizures, so part of the drop is a reporting gap, not only attrition.

answers.q: Are plants trafficked as much as animals?
answers.a: Plants are 15% of seized shipments reported to CITES but only 10% of news cases: timber, orchids and medicinal plants are trafficked far more than they are reported.

answers.limit: CITES lists many more plant species than news ever names; plant blindness cuts both ways.

answers.q: What is seized at US ports, and where does it come from?
answers.a: US wildlife inspectors seized 19,346 import records of the groups WildTrace follows; most came from China, Indonesia, Mexico.

answers.q: Does wildlife trade overlap with disease outbreaks?
answers.a: Viruses confirmed by sequencing or isolation are recorded in 23 traded groups, and WHO published 2,118 reports on diseases with an animal reservoir; the two share a map, not a cause.

number.k: WHO outbreak reports on animal-borne disease

answers.limit: Virus records follow where scientists sampled; an outbreak near a seizure does not mean the trade caused it.

answers.q: Is wildlife crime a national security risk?
answers.a: It reaches security through seven links, from extraction to crime revenue, disease and ecosystem loss; the weakest in open data is who profits.
